dedupe_keys.name: doe ev data collection charging data livewire

description: The DOE EV Data Collection charging data record charging sessions of electric vehicles in commercial fleets, covering light-, medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, public transit and off-road equipment. Charging data come from the charger (EVSE) software, the vehicle's onboard systems or a utility submeter, and the source can be told from the pattern of anonymous charger, vehicle and fleet ids. Tables give daily or per-session charging parameters, charger attributes and vehicle attributes, each with a data dictionary, so vehicle ids link charging sessions to vehicles and chargers. The collection is sponsored by the DOE Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy's Vehicle Technologies Office, credits CALSTART authors and involves NREL, PNNL and INL, and is hosted on the Livewire data platform with the DOI 10.15483/1989855. Coverage is US commercial fleets. Access: listed on OSTI and linked to Livewire; the Livewire pages are a JavaScript application whose access terms were not readable on 26 September 2026, while a third-party catalogue lists it as public domain. Caveats: data were uploaded quarterly and subject to change until the project ended, and the parameters vary by vehicle and charger. It supports electric fleet charging demand modelling, depot capacity planning and grid-transport interaction studies, and complements the European truck charging demand datasets catalogued here.
